content: The FBI, the EPA, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) have stopped short of officially blaming Iran for a spate of cyberattacks on Minnesota’s water systems, but consensus is that Iran is likely behind them. That, of course, hasn’t stopped Donald Trump from sharing his own theory — that Governor Tim Walz is to blame and telling reporters that “I don’t think there was an Iranian cyberattack.” Trump’s comments come shortly after the FBI issued a warning that the cyberattacks on American infrastructure were spreading to other states. In Minnesota alone, at least 30 community water systems had been targeted in what appeared to be a coordinated attack. The CISA has linked similar attacks earlier in the year to Iran, which has been the target of an on-again-off-again war waged by the US government. With limited military options, Iran has repeatedly turned to digital efforts to become a thorn in the side of the Trump administration and wage a PR war. Trump has lashed out frequently at Minnesota and Walz during his second term and even threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act against it during a surge of ICE enforcement efforts in the state that left multiple people dead.

chineseContent: 美国联邦调查局 (FBI)、美国环保局 (EPA) 以及网络安全和基础设施安全局 (CISA) 并未正式指责伊朗对明尼苏达州供水系统发动一系列网络攻击，但共识是伊朗很可能是幕后黑手。当然，这并没有阻止唐纳德·特朗普分享他自己的理论——州长蒂姆·沃尔兹应该受到指责，并告诉记者“我不认为伊朗发生了网络攻击”。特朗普发表此番言论之前不久，联邦调查局发出警告，称针对美国基础设施的网络攻击正在蔓延到其他州。仅在明尼苏达州，至少有 30 个社区供水系统成为了这次似乎是协同攻击的目标。 CISA 将今年早些时候的类似袭击与伊朗联系起来，伊朗一直是美国政府时断时续发动战争的目标。由于军事选择有限，伊朗一再转向数字化努力，成为特朗普政府的眼中钉，并发动公关战。特朗普在第二任期内经常猛烈抨击明尼苏达州和沃尔兹州，甚至在该州 ICE 执法力度激增导致多人死亡期间威胁要援引《叛乱法》来对付它们。
